Definition: from the same as G2218; a couple, i.e. a team (of oxen yoked together) or brace (of birds tied together):--yoke, pair.
BiblicalUsage: A yoke, a pair — two oxen under one yoke, two turtledoves for an offering — is what the word means. Mary brings a pair of turtledoves for her purification, and in the parable a man has bought five yoke of oxen and cannot come to the supper. The pair is ordinary life, and ordinary life keeps getting in the way.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the yoke in the parable is honest: good, ordinary things become excuses the moment they outrank the invitation.
